title: Breakdown of unitarity in the dimensional reduction scheme
claim: Beta functions in different schemes should be related by finite coupling redefinitions; in non-SUSY gauge theories DRED fails this test; the culprit is the counterterm structure needed for overlapping divergences, which violates unitarity. SUSY theories (N=2, N=4 gauge theories, any SUSY theory without vector field) are not affected because the epsilon-scalar renormalizes like the scalar, fermion and vector fields.
loop_order: multi-loop (overlapping divergences, i.e. from two loops)
theory: non-SUSY gauge theories; SUSY theories as stated exceptions
scheme: DRED in which the counterterms of the 4-dimensional couplings are reused for the epsilon-scalar couplings (called 'System 4' in S2.08).
symmetry_argument: Not a SUSY argument; consistency of scheme change by coupling redefinition (unitarity).

proved: With epsilon-scalar couplings identified with gauge couplings in non-SUSY theories, DRED is not related to DREG by a coupling redefinition.

evidence: Response: S2.08 hep-ph/9401349 Sec. 1 and 3 (separate evanescent couplings renormalized so that Green functions with external epsilon-scalars are finite restore equivalence and unitarity).
red_flags: The conclusion is specific to the identification of evanescent with real couplings; it is the origin of the rule that evanescent couplings must be kept separate (S2.11, S2.14).
Abstract names N=2, N=4 and vector-free SUSY theories as unaffected; N=1 gauge theories with matter are not named in the abstract.
cross_checks: S2.11_HKMS2006 (concrete three-loop consequence of identifying alpha_e = alpha_s)
